senses.gloss:
रभ् रभ् (originally connected with rts.
ग्रभ्, लभ्), cl. 1. A. (in poetry also P.)
रभते (-ति), रेभे, रप्स्यते, अरब्ध, रब्धुम्,
to seize, take (Ved.); to take hold of, clasp, embrace;
to desire vehemently, regret; to act rashly: Pass.
रभ्यते, अरम्भि: Caus. रम्भयति, -यितुम्,
Aor. अररम्भत्: Desid. रिप्सते: Intens. रार-
भ्यते, रारम्भीति, रारब्धि; [cf. Gr. ῥώννυμι,
λαμβάνω: Lat. rabies, robur: Goth. arbaiths, li-
ban: Angl. Sax. earfedh, earfodh, leofian, lifian,
lybban, (perhaps also) a-refian, ‘to bear;’ a-rœfnan,
‘to take away:’ Old Germ. laba, labôn.]

रभ, अस्, m., N. of an ape (in Rāmāyaṇa IV.
33, 14).

रभस्, अस्, n. violence, impetuosity, (रभसा,
with impetuosity, violently), zeal; force, energy,
power, strength, strengthening food, oblation (Ved.).
—रभस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. possessing impe-
tuosity, violent, impetuous, zealous.
—रभो-दा, आस्,
आस्, अम्, Ved. bestowing strength or force, (Sāy. =
बलस्य दातृ.)

रभस, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. रभस् above), impe-
tuous, violent, rapid, fierce, wild; eager; powerful,
strong, energetic; strengthening, invigorating (Ved.);
joyful; (अस्), m. violence, impetuosity, vehemence,
haste, speed, velocity, precipitation, (रभसात् or
रभसेन, with violence, impetuously, in great
haste, quickly); passion, anger, ill temper, rage;
passionate fondness; joy, pleasure; regret, sorrow;
N. of a magical incantation recited over weapons;
of a Dānava; of a king (son of Rambha); of a
lexicographer; of a Rākṣasa; of an ape (in Rāmā-
yaṇa IV. 39,7).
—रभस-पाल, अस्, m., N. of a
lexicographer.

रभसान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = रभस, impe-
tuous, violent, rapid.

रभि, इस्, f., Ved. (according to some) a particu-
lar part of a car or chariot, (but according to Sāy.,
Ṛg-veda VIII. 5, 29, रभि is an adj. = आरम्भ-
णीय or आलम्भन-भूत, ‘supporting.’)

रभिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. most violent or
impetuous, very strong.

रभीयस् or रभ्यस्, आन्, असी, अस्, Ved. more
impetuous, very strong.

रभेणक रभेणक, अस्, m., N. of a serpent-
demon.

राभस्य राभस्य, अम्, n. (fr. रभस), velo-
city, impetuosity; eagerness, delight, joy, pleasure.
